key_insight: The paper introduces Asymptotics Learning Theory, using optimization to recover unknown constants in asymptotic expansions with provable convergence-rate guarantees.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled way to estimate asymptotic parameters from numerical data, which can improve model calibration and long-horizon prediction in computational science workflows.
method: Sliding Linear Least Squares (sLLSQ) for estimating unknown asymptotic constants.
Sliding Tikhonov Linear Least Squares (sT-LLSQ) as a regularized variant for improved stability.
Rigorous asymptotic analysis to derive sufficient convergence conditions and rate bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs plus numerical examples that verify the convergence results and illustrate applications in analytic combinatorics.
watch_item: Both methods can converge slowly and may even diverge in some cases, so windowing and regularization choices must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Learning Asymptotics with Convergence-Rate Guarantees using Linear Least Squares
